newsitem.title: USA: U.S. banks match or exceed Q2 earnings forecasts.
newsitem.headline: U.S. banks match or exceed Q2 earnings forecasts.

text.p: Several U.S. banking companies Monday reported second-quarter earnings higher than a year ago and in line with or slightly above expectations.
Analysts said strong fee income contributed to the gains and credit quality overall was in good shape.
"It looks like most banks are meeting or are slightly above expectations," said Michael Mayo, analyst at Credit Suisse First Boston.

In the case of Bank of New York Co Inc -- which reported a nine percent rise in net income to $269 million, excluding special items a year ago -- analyst David Berry of Keefe, Bruyette & Woods Inc noted that the company is "re-orienting itself away from its crdit card business with increasing emphasis on securities processing."
Bank of New York said its securities process revenue rose 18 percent to $190 million.
Bank of New York also noted that after the end of the quarter a "substantial loan" to a retailer became nonperforming.
A Bank of New York spokesman identified the retailer as Montgomery Ward Holding Corp, which filed for bankruptcy July 7.
Documents in the Montgomery Ward bankruptcy filing list Bank of New York as one of the 20 largest unsecured creditors with a claim of $155.2 million.
"We expect a third of that might be secured exposure," Berry said.
NationsBank Corp, the fourth-largest U.S. bank based on assets, reported second-quarter net income rose 26 percent from a year-ago to $762 million.

Harold Schroeder, analyst at Keefe, Bruyette & Woods, said the acquisition of Boatmen's Bancshares completed early this year was a strong contributor to the earnings improvement. He said the bank's expense reductions were running ahead of original targets. But he noted that with the NationsBank share price high, the company had to borrow more money to continue its program of buying back 40 percent of the shares issued in the Boatmen's acquisition.
"Overall it was a strong quarter," Schroeder said of NatonsBank. "Non-interest revenues were the real key to this quarter, along with lower costs."

Mayo noted there were some positive surprises in credit quality. "First Chicago NBD Corp's credit card losses were not as high as we thought and asset quality was better-than-expected at the Norwest Corp consumer finance subsidiary," he said.

Minneapolis-based Norwest reported second-quarter net income rose 16.1 percent from a year ago to $331.4 million. In the Norwest Financial consumer unit, second-quarter earnings rose to $66.4 million from $65.4 million a year ago and $61.6 million in the first quarter of 1997.
The increase from the first quarter was prmarily due to reduced loan charge-offs which fell $8.4 millon to $58.6 million, Norwest said.

First Chicago NBD reported net income rose to $378 million in the second quarter from $361 million a year ago. Per-share earnings rose 10 percent to a record $1.20 per share diluted from $1.09 a year ago.

Chairman Verne Istock said in a statment it was encouraging that credit card charge-offs were flat with the first quarter's. He noted the positive effects of fee revenue growth and an aggressive stock repurchase program.
The net charge-off ratio for First Chicago NBD's managed credit card portfolio was 7.7 percent, compared with 5.9 percent a year ago and 7.4 percent in the first quarter of 1997.

Cleveland-based National City Corp reported second quarter net income rose 11.1 percent to $0.90 per share. In a statement, chairman and chief executive David Daberko cited fee income growth, "excellent credit qualty" and expense control.

In early afternoon, Bank of New York was up 1/2 to 46-1/8, Norwest was off 5/16 to 59-7/8, First Chicago NBD was up 1-1/16 to 64-1/6, NationsBank was up 1-3/16 to 67-13/16 and National City Corp was off 5/8 to 54-1/4.
